title: Note to the Employer Statement: The Refundable Credit Balance
content:
**The amount.** On the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, the refund an employer may request is the credit balance shown on its account, that is the balance due taken as a positive amount when it is negative and nothing when it is not, rounded to the cent.

The balance due is the amount the employer owes: contributions, reimbursement bills, penalties and interest assessed, less payments and credits. A negative balance due is a credit owed to the employer.

## Reading the balance due

| Balance due shown on the account | Credit balance | Refund the employer may request |
|---|---|---|
| Negative, USD -1,234.56 | USD 1,234.56 | USD 1,234.56 |
| Negative, USD -0.40 | USD 0.40 | USD 0.40 |
| Zero | Nothing | USD 0.00 |
| Positive, USD 312.00 | Nothing | USD 0.00 |

## Questions answered by this note

**Is the amount ever taken from a single quarter rather than the whole account?** No. It is the credit balance of the account as a whole, read from the balance due.

**When is the figure rounded?** To the cent, once, on the amount requested.

**Hypothetical statement.** An employer's statement shows contributions and interest assessed of USD 8,410.00 against payments and credits of USD 9,105.25. The balance due is USD -695.25, a credit; the refund the employer may request is USD 695.25.
